document.abstract: The SMPTE Motion Imaging Journal has reported frequently on standardization activities for transmission of digital TV. This report has been jointly prepared by the leaders of ATSC and DVB to mark the creation of the FOBTV initiative, which brings together not just ATSC and DVB but also many other organizations from around the world with an active interest in digital TV.

authors.bio: Philip Laven is chairman of the DVB Project, acting on behalf of the European Broadcasting Union (EBU) where he was director of the Technical Department from May 1997 until August 2007. Before joining the EBU, he worked for the British Broadcasting Corp. (BBC) where most of his work was associated with R&D, including being Chief Engineer R&D with responsibility for all of the BBC's R&D activities. As controller of engineering policy from 1993 to 1997, he played a leading role in the development of the BBC's policy on many technical developments, such as the introduction of digital audio broadcasting and digital television. Between 1994 and 2009, he was chairman of the ETSI/EBU/CENELEC Joint Technical Committee (which is responsible for setting European standards for broadcasting systems). In April 2012, he was appointed vice-chairman of the FOBTV initiative.
authors.name: Philip Laven

authors.bio: Mark Richer is the president of the Advanced Television Systems Committee, Inc. (ATSC). The ATSC is an international, nonprofit organization developing voluntary standards for digital television. Richer first joined the ATSC after 16 years with the Public Broadcasting Service (PBS) where, as vice president of engineering & computer services, he was responsible for development of new technologies for PBS and its member stations. — Richer was the 2010 recipient of the National Association of Broadcasters Engineering Achievement Award for Television and a recipient of Broadcast & Cable's Technology Leadership Award in 2007. He is a Fellow of SMPTE and serves on the FCC Technology Advisory Council. Richer is the chairman of the Future of Broadcast TV (FOBTV) initiative. He holds two patents and has a BS degree from the Rochester Institute of Technology.
authors.name: Mark Richer
